source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Aramaic. **MAJOR TEXTUAL DIVERGENCE**: chapter 4 (MT 3:31–4:34) is the chapter with the most substantial OG-vs-MT divergence in the entire book. The OG is significantly shorter (lacks much of the autobiographical first-person framing), reorders material, and presents the madness-narrative differently. Theodotion-Greek conforms to MT. The Prayer of Nabonidus from Qumran (4Q242) preserves a parallel tradition in which a different Babylonian king (Nabonidus, not Nebuchadnezzar) is afflicted at Teima for seven years — widely regarded as a closer-to-historical original of the tradition (Nebuchadnezzar's name appears to have replaced Nabonidus in the canonical form). SECONDARY: 4Q112 (Daniela) preserves fragments; 4Q113 (Danielb) preserves portions. TERTIARY: Greek versions (Ziegler-Munnich 1999) consulted at all major divergence points.

source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 4 — ARAMAIC, the tree-dream and Nebuchadnezzar's madness. **VERSE NUMBERING**: BHS numbers this chapter 3:31–4:34; English/Vulgate numbers it 4:1–37. This file follows BHS numbering but cross-maps to English 4:1–37 (BHS 3:31 = English 4:1; BHS 4:1 = English 4:4 etc.). The chapter is uniquely autobiographical — narrated in the first person by Nebuchadnezzar himself (vv 1-18, 34-37), with a third-person interlude (vv 19-33) covering the madness-period when the king could not narrate. **The OG-vs-MT divergence is substantial**: OG presents a shorter, differently-ordered version. The Qumran 4Q242 Prayer of Nabonidus preserves what is likely the closer-to-historical original — a tradition about Nabonidus's Teima exile (553-543 BCE), transferred in the canonical Daniel form to the more famous Nebuchadnezzar.

verses.text: נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א לְֽכָל־עַֽמְמַיָּ֞א אֻמַיָּ֧א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֛א דִּֽי־דארין דָיְרִ֥ין בְּכָל־אַרְעָ֖א שְׁלָמְכ֥וֹן יִשְׂגֵּֽא׃
verses.translit: Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ lə-ḵol-ʿammə-mayyāʾ ʾummayyāʾ wə-liššānayyāʾ dî-ḏāyərîn bə-ḵol-ʾarʿāʾ šəlāməḵōn yiśgēʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 3:31 (= English 4:1; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **King Nebuchadnezzar to all peoples, nations, and languages that dwell in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you!** **VERSE NUMBERING**: BHS 3:31 = English 4:1. This is an encyclical-letter opening — the entire chapter is framed as a royal proclamation. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. 1 Pet 1:2 + 2 Pet 1:2 ('grace and peace be multiplied' — χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη πληθυνθείη) — the NT epistolary opening directly inherits the Aramaic šəlāməḵōn yiśgēʾ formula. cf. Jude 2. The universalizing tripartite formula 'peoples, nations, languages' continues from ch 3. Qere-ketiv: דארין/דָיְרִין (qere).

verses.text: אָֽתַיָּא֙ וְתִמְהַיָּ֔א דִּ֚י עֲבַ֣ד עִמִּ֔י אֱלָהָ֖א עִלָּאָ֑ה שְׁפַ֥ר קָֽדָמַ֖י לְהַחֲוָיָֽה׃
verses.translit: ʾāṯayyāʾ wə-ṯimhayyāʾ dī ʿăḇaḏ ʿimmî ʾĕlāhāʾ ʿillāʾāh šəpar qodāmay lə-haḥăwāyāh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 3:32 (= English 4:2; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **It has seemed good to me to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has wrought toward me.** **TERM**: אָתַיָּא וְתִמְהַיָּא (ʾāṯayyāʾ wə-ṯimhayyāʾ 'signs and wonders') — Aramaic equivalent of Hebrew אוֹתוֹת וּמוֹפְתִים. **CROSS-CORPUS**: 'signs and wonders' is the Exodus-formula (Deut 4:34, 6:22, 7:19, 26:8, 29:3, 34:11); the NT applies it to apostolic miracles (Acts 2:22, 2:43, 4:30, 5:12, 14:3, 15:12; Heb 2:4). **TITLE**: אֱלָהָא עִלָּאָה (Most High God) — see 3:26.

verses.text: אָת֙וֹהִי֙ כְּמָ֣ה רַבְרְבִ֔ין וְתִמְה֖וֹהִי כְּמָ֣ה תַקִּיפִ֑ין מַלְכוּתֵהּ֙ מַלְכ֣וּת עָלַ֔ם וְשָׁלְטָנֵ֖הּ עִם־דָּ֥ר וְדָֽר׃
verses.translit: ʾāṯōhî kəmāh raḇrəḇîn wə-ṯimhōhî kəmāh ṯaqqîpîn malḵūṯēh malḵūṯ ʿālam wə-šolṭānēh ʿim-dār wə-ḏār
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 3:33 (= English 4:3; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **How great are his signs, how mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion endures from generation to generation.** **THE EVERLASTING-KINGDOM REFRAIN**: מַלְכוּת עָלַם (malḵūṯ ʿālam) — appears here, 4:34, 6:26, 7:14, 7:27 — the central theological assertion of the Aramaic Daniel. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Ps 145:13 ('your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom'); cf. Luke 1:33 ('of his kingdom there shall be no end'); cf. Rev 11:15 ('the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord... and he shall reign forever and ever') — direct Daniel-Aramaic inheritance.

verses.text: אֲנָ֣ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר שְׁלֵ֤ה הֲוֵית֙ בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְרַעְנַ֖ן בְּהֵיכְלִֽי׃
verses.translit: ʾănāh Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar šəlēh hăwêṯ bə-ḇêṯî wə-raʿnan bə-hêḵəlî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:1 (= English 4:4; Aramaic)
verses.witness_tertiary: OG significantly shorter; the autobiographical first-person framing is largely absent in OG
verses.notes: **I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and prospering in my palace.** **FIRST-PERSON ROYAL NARRATIVE** begins. The 'at ease' setting establishes hubris-before-fall structure. **OG DIVERGENCE**: OG version lacks much of this first-person framing — Collins 1993 argues the MT first-person frame is secondary, added to enhance the conversion-testimony genre.

verses.text: חֵ֥לֶם חֲזֵ֖ית וִֽידַחֲלִנַּ֑נִי וְהַרְהֹרִין֙ עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבִ֔י וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י יְבַהֲלֻנַּֽנִי׃
verses.translit: ḥēlem ḥăzêṯ wî-ḏaḥălinnannî wə-harhōrîn ʿal-miškəḇî wə-ḥezwê rēšî yəḇahălunnannî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:2 (= English 4:5; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **I saw a dream which made me afraid; the fancies on my bed and the visions of my head troubled me.** Parallel to 2:1 — the king is troubled by another dream. The narrative pattern repeats: dream → mantic-class failure → Daniel's interpretation.

verses.text: וּמִנִּי֙ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵ֔ם לְהַנְעָלָ֣ה קָֽדָמַ֔י לְכֹ֖ל חַכִּימֵ֣י בָבֶ֑ל דִּֽי־פְשַׁ֥ר חֶלְמָ֖א יְהֽוֹדְעֻנַּֽנִי׃
verses.translit: ū-minnî śîm ṭəʿēm lə-hanʿālāh qodāmay lə-ḵōl ḥakkîmê Bāḇel dî-pəšar ḥelmāʾ yəhōḏəʿunnannî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:3 (= English 4:6; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Therefore I made a decree that all the wise men of Babylon should be brought before me, to make known to me the interpretation of the dream.**

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֣יִן עללין עָֽלִּ֗ין חַרְטֻמַּיָּא֙ אָֽשְׁפַיָּ֔א כשדיא כַּשְׂדָּאֵ֖י וְגָזְרַיָּ֑א וְחֶלְמָ֗א אָמַ֤ר אֲנָה֙ קֳדָ֣מֵיה֔וֹן וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ לָא־מְהוֹדְעִ֥ין לִֽי׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin ʿāllîn ḥarṭummayyāʾ ʾāšəpayyāʾ kaśdāʾê wə-ḡāzərayyāʾ wə-ḥelmāʾ ʾāmar ʾănāh qodāmêhōn ū-pišrēh lāʾ-məhōḏəʿîn lî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:4 (= English 4:7; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and astrologers came in; and I told them the dream, but they could not make known to me its interpretation.** Four mantic classes (cf. 2:2, 5:7). Qere-ketiv: עללין/עָלִּין (qere); כשדיא/כַּשְׂדָּאֵי (qere). **TERM**: גָּזְרַיָּא (gāzərayyāʾ 'astrologers' lit. 'determiners') — Persian-period diviner-class designation.

verses.text: וְעַ֣ד אָחֳרֵ֡ין עַל֩ קָֽדָמַ֨י דָּנִיֵּ֜אל דִּֽי־שְׁמֵ֤הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ כְּשֻׁ֣ם אֱלָהִ֔י וְדִ֛י רֽוּחַ־אֱלָהִ֥ין קַדִּישִׁ֖ין בֵּ֑הּ וְחֶלְמָ֖א קָֽדָמ֥וֹהִי אַמְרֵֽת׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿaḏ ʾoḥŏrên ʿal qodāmay Dāniyyēʾl dî-šəmēh Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar kə-šum ʾĕlāhî wə-ḏî rûaḥ-ʾĕlāhîn qaddîšîn bēh wə-ḥelmāʾ qodāmōhî ʾamrēṯ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:5 (= English 4:8; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **At last Daniel came in before me — he who was named Belteshazzar after the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods — and I told him the dream.** **KEY PHRASE**: רוּחַ אֱלָהִין קַדִּישִׁין (rûaḥ ʾĕlāhîn qaddîšîn 'the spirit of the holy gods' — plural ʾĕlāhîn). Polytheistic framing preserved (Nebuchadnezzar is speaking). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Gen 41:38 (Pharaoh on Joseph: 'a man in whom is the spirit of God') — the Joseph-pattern is being deployed. **NAME**: בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר (Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar) — Akkadian *Bēl-balāṭ-uṣur* 'Bel protect his life'; the king's deity Bel/Marduk is encoded in the name.

verses.text: בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֮ רַ֣ב חַרְטֻמַּיָּא֒ דִּ֣י ׀ אֲנָ֣ה יִדְעֵ֗ת דִּ֠י ר֣וּחַ אֱלָהִ֤ין קַדִּישִׁין֙ בָּ֔ךְ וְכָל־רָ֖ז לָא־אָנֵ֣ס לָ֑ךְ חֶזְוֵ֨י חֶלְמִ֧י דִֽי־חֲזֵ֛ית וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ אֱמַֽר׃
verses.translit: Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar raḇ ḥarṭummayyāʾ dī ʾănāh yiḏʿēṯ dī rûaḥ ʾĕlāhîn qaddîšîn bāḵ wə-ḵol-rāz lāʾ-ʾānēs lāḵ ḥezwê ḥelmî ḏî-ḥăzêṯ ū-pišrēh ʾĕmar
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:6 (= English 4:9; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'O Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no mystery is difficult for you, here is the dream which I saw; tell me its interpretation.'** **TERM**: רָז (rāz 'mystery') — Persian loanword; the Daniel-Aramaic technical term for apocalyptic mystery. Reappears in 2:18-19, 2:27-30, 2:47, 4:9. **CROSS-CORPUS**: the Qumran sectarian use of רָז (1QpHab, 1QS) and the NT μυστήριον (Mark 4:11; Rom 16:25; 1 Cor 2:7; Eph 3:3-6; Col 1:26-27; Rev 1:20, 10:7, 17:5, 17:7) both inherit this Daniel-Aramaic technical-apocalyptic vocabulary.

verses.text: וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבִ֑י חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית וַאֲל֥וּ אִילָ֛ן בְּג֥וֹא אַרְעָ֖א וְרוּמֵ֥הּ שַׂגִּֽיא׃
verses.translit: wə-ḥezwê rēšî ʿal-miškəḇî ḥāzēh hăwêṯ wa-ʾălū ʾîlān bə-ḡōʾ ʾarʿāʾ wə-rūmēh śaggîʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:7 (= English 4:10; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **The visions of my head as I lay in bed were these: I saw, and behold, a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height was great.** **THE COSMIC-TREE DREAM**: the *axis mundi* tree-image is widely attested in ANE iconography (Assyrian sacred tree, Babylonian *kiškanu*). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Ezek 31 (Pharaoh-as-cedar); cf. Ezek 17 (the cedar-twig); cf. 1 En 24-25 (the tree of life on the cosmic mountain). The image-of-king-as-tree is a standard ANE royal-ideology trope.

verses.text: רְבָ֥ה אִֽילָנָ֖א וּתְקִ֑ף וְרוּמֵהּ֙ יִמְטֵ֣א לִשְׁמַיָּ֔א וַחֲזוֹתֵ֖הּ לְס֥וֹף כָּל־אַרְעָֽא׃
verses.translit: rəḇāh ʾîlānāʾ ū-ṯəqip wə-rūmēh yimṭēʾ li-šmayyāʾ wa-ḥăzōṯēh lə-sōp̄ kol-ʾarʿāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:8 (= English 4:11; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **The tree grew and became strong, and its top reached to heaven, and it was visible to the end of the whole earth.** **COSMIC AXIS**: 'top reached to heaven' echoes Gen 11:4 (Babel tower) — the Babylonian-king-tree IS the Babel-tower in dream-form, per Newsom 2014.

verses.text: עָפְיֵ֤הּ שַׁפִּיר֙ וְאִנְבֵּ֣הּ שַׂגִּ֔יא וּמָז֨וֹן לְכֹ֖לָּא־בֵ֑הּ תְּחֹת֜וֹהִי תַּטְלֵ֣ל ׀ חֵיוַ֣ת בָּרָ֗א וּבְעַנְפ֙וֹהִי֙ ידרון יְדוּרָן֙ צִפֲּרֵ֣י שְׁמַיָּ֔א וּמִנֵּ֖הּ יִתְּזִ֥ין כָּל־בִּשְׂרָֽא׃
verses.translit: ʿopyēh šappîr wə-ʾinbēh śaggîʾ ū-māzōn lə-ḵōllāʾ-ḇēh təḥōṯōhî taṭlēl ḥêwaṯ bārāʾ ū-ḇə-ʿanpōhî yəḏūrān ṣippărê šəmayyāʾ ū-minnēh yittəzîn kol-biśrāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:9 (= English 4:12; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Its foliage was fair, and its fruit abundant, and in it was food for all; the beasts of the field found shade under it, and the birds of the air dwelt in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.** **CROSS-CORPUS**: the language ('birds of the air... in its branches') is precisely echoed in Jesus' mustard-seed parable (Matt 13:32 / Mark 4:32 / Luke 13:19) — the kingdom-as-tree-sheltering-birds is direct Daniel inheritance. Qere-ketiv: ידרון/יְדוּרָן (qere).

verses.text: חָזֵ֥ה הֲוֵ֛ית בְּחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבִ֑י וַאֲלוּ֙ עִ֣יר וְקַדִּ֔ישׁ מִן־שְׁמַיָּ֖א נָחִֽת׃
verses.translit: ḥāzēh hăwêṯ bə-ḥezwê rēšî ʿal-miškəḇî wa-ʾălū ʿîr wə-qaddîš min-šəmayyāʾ nāḥiṯ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:10 (= English 4:13; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **I saw in the visions of my head as I lay in bed, and behold, a watcher, a holy one, came down from heaven.** **KEY TERM**: עִיר (ʿîr 'watcher') — appears only in Aramaic Daniel (4:13, 4:17, 4:23) in the canonical HB but is foundational for Second-Temple angelology. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: the 'watchers' (ʿîrîn, Greek ἐγρήγοροι) are central to: (a) 1 En 6-16 (Book of the Watchers — the rebel-angels who father the giants/Nephilim of Gen 6); (b) Jubilees 4:15, 4:22, 5:1; (c) CD-A 2:18 (the Damascus Document); (d) 4Q180-181, 4Q201ff (Aramaic Enoch fragments). The Daniel watchers are *good* watchers; the Enochic watchers are fallen. The Daniel-Aramaic preserves the term in its original neutral sense ('the wakeful ones'), which the Enochic tradition then specializes as the rebel-angels. **CROSS-CORPUS to NT**: Jude 6 + 2 Pet 2:4 inherit the Enochic-watchers tradition directly.

verses.text: קָרֵ֨א בְחַ֜יִל וְכֵ֣ן אָמַ֗ר גֹּ֤דּוּ אִֽילָנָא֙ וְקַצִּ֣צוּ עַנְפ֔וֹהִי אַתַּ֥רוּ עָפְיֵ֖הּ וּבַדַּ֣רוּ אִנְבֵּ֑הּ תְּנֻ֤ד חֵֽיוְתָא֙ מִן־תַּחְתּ֔וֹהִי וְצִפֲּרַיָּ֖א מִן־עַנְפֽוֹהִי׃
verses.translit: qārēʾ ḇə-ḥayil wə-ḵēn ʾāmar gōddū ʾîlānāʾ wə-qaṣṣiṣū ʿanpōhî ʾattarū ʿopyēh ū-ḇaddarū ʾinbēh tənuḏ ḥêwəṯāʾ min-taḥtōhî wə-ṣippărayyāʾ min-ʿanpōhî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:11 (= English 4:14; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **He cried aloud and said: 'Cut down the tree and chop off its branches, strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit; let the beasts flee from under it and the birds from its branches.'** The watcher's decree.

verses.text: בְּרַ֨ם עִקַּ֤ר שָׁרְשׁ֙וֹהִי֙ בְּאַרְעָ֣א שְׁבֻ֔קוּ וּבֶֽאֱסוּר֙ דִּֽי־פַרְזֶ֣ל וּנְחָ֔שׁ בְּדִתְאָ֖א דִּ֣י בָרָ֑א וּבְטַ֤ל שְׁמַיָּא֙ יִצְטַבַּ֔ע וְעִם־חֵיוְתָ֥א חֲלָקֵ֖הּ בַּעֲשַׂ֥ב אַרְעָֽא׃
verses.translit: bəram ʿiqqar šoršōhî bə-ʾarʿāʾ šəḇuqū ū-ḇe-ʾĕsūr dî-p̄arzel ū-nəḥāš bə-ḏiṯʾāʾ dī ḇārāʾ ū-ḇə-ṭal šəmayyāʾ yiṣṭabbaʿ wə-ʿim-ḥêwəṯāʾ ḥălāqēh ba-ʿăśaḇ ʾarʿāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:12 (= English 4:15; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'But leave the stump of its roots in the earth, bound with a band of iron and bronze, amid the tender grass of the field; let him be wet with the dew of heaven, and let his lot be with the beasts in the grass of the earth.'** **PRONOUN SHIFT**: the dream-language transitions from neuter 'it' (the tree) to masculine 'him' — the tree IS a person. The iron-bronze band suggests fettering. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. 4Q242 Prayer of Nabonidus, where Nabonidus is afflicted with a 'severe inflammation' for seven years at Teima — the Qumran parallel preserves the seven-year affliction-motif but with different specifics.

verses.text: לִבְבֵהּ֙ מִן־אֲנוֹשָׁ֣א ישנון יְשַׁנּ֔וֹן וּלְבַ֥ב חֵיוָ֖ה יִתְיְהִ֣ב לֵ֑הּ וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֥וּן עֲלֽוֹהִי׃
verses.translit: liḇḇēh min-ʾănōšāʾ yəšannōn ū-ləḇaḇ ḥêwāh yiṯyəhiḇ lēh wə-šiḇʿāh ʿiddānîn yaḥləp̄ūn ʿălōhî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:13 (= English 4:16; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'Let his mind be changed from a man's, and let a beast's mind be given to him; and let seven times pass over him.'** **THE SEVEN-TIMES (שִׁבְעָה עִדָּנִין šiḇʿāh ʿiddānîn)**: critical apocalyptic-chronological term. עִדָּן (ʿiddān 'time/season') is the same word used in 7:25 ('time, times, and half a time') and arguably 12:7. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. 4Q242 Prayer of Nabonidus ('seven years'); cf. Rev 12:14 ('a time, times, and half a time') — the Daniel-Aramaic ʿiddān vocabulary undergirds the entire apocalyptic chronology tradition. The 'beast's mind' / lycanthropy / boanthropy: Collins 1993 reads as the literary deployment of a known psychiatric condition (clinical lycanthropy).

verses.text: בִּגְזֵרַ֤ת עִירִין֙ פִּתְגָמָ֔א וּמֵאמַ֥ר קַדִּישִׁ֖ין שְׁאֵֽלְתָ֑א עַד־דִּבְרַ֡ת דִּ֣י יִנְדְּע֣וּן חַ֠יַּיָּא דִּֽי־שַׁלִּ֨יט עליא עִלָּאָ֜ה בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אנושא אֲנָשָׁ֗א וּלְמַן־דִּ֤י יִצְבֵּא֙ יִתְּנִנַּ֔הּ וּשְׁפַ֥ל אֲנָשִׁ֖ים יְקִ֥ים עֲלַֽיהּ׃
verses.translit: bi-ḡzēraṯ ʿîrîn piṯḡāmāʾ ū-mēʾmar qaddîšîn šəʾēltāʾ ʿaḏ-dibraṯ dî yindəʿūn ḥayyayyāʾ dî-šallîṭ ʿillāʾāh bə-malḵūṯ ʾănāšāʾ ū-lə-man-dî yiṣbēʾ yittəninnah ū-šəp̄al ʾănāšîm yəqîm ʿălah
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:14 (= English 4:17; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'The sentence is by the decree of the watchers, the decision by the word of the holy ones, to the end that the living may know that the Most High rules the kingdom of men, and gives it to whom he will, and sets over it the lowliest of men.'** **THE WATCHERS AS HEAVENLY COURT**: the decree comes from the עִירִין וְקַדִּישִׁין (ʿîrîn wə-qaddîšîn 'watchers and holy ones') as a council. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. 1 En 14 (the throne-vision); cf. 1 Kgs 22 (Micaiah's heavenly council); cf. Job 1-2. **The thematic refrain** — 'the Most High rules the kingdom of men, and gives it to whom he will' — recurs in 4:25, 4:32, 5:21. Qere-ketiv: עליא/עִלָּאָה; אנושא/אֲנָשָׁא.

verses.text: דְּנָה֙ חֶלְמָ֣א חֲזֵ֔ית אֲנָ֖ה מַלְכָּ֣א נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֑ר ואנתה וְאַ֨נְתְּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֜ר פִּשְׁרֵ֣א ׀ אֱמַ֗ר כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּ֣י ׀ כָּל־חַכִּימֵ֣י מַלְכוּתִ֗י לָֽא־יָכְלִ֤ין פִּשְׁרָא֙ לְהוֹדָ֣עֻתַ֔נִי ואנתה וְאַ֣נְתְּ כָּהֵ֔ל דִּ֛י רֽוּחַ־אֱלָהִ֥ין קַדִּישִׁ֖ין בָּֽךְ׃
verses.translit: dənāh ḥelmāʾ ḥăzêṯ ʾănāh malkāʾ Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar wə-ʾant Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar pišrāʾ ʾĕmar kol-qŏḇēl dī kol-ḥakkîmê malḵūṯî lāʾ-yāḵəlîn pišrāʾ lə-hōḏāʿuṯanî wə-ʾant kāhēl dī rûaḥ-ʾĕlāhîn qaddîšîn bāḵ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:15 (= English 4:18; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. And you, O Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able, for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.'** End of first-person section (vv 1-18). Qere-ketiv (twice): ואנתה/וְאַנְתְּ (qere).

verses.text: אֱדַ֨יִן דָּֽנִיֵּ֜אל דִּֽי־שְׁמֵ֣הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֗ר אֶשְׁתּוֹמַם֙ כְּשָׁעָ֣ה חֲדָ֔ה וְרַעְיֹנֹ֖הִי יְבַהֲלֻנֵּ֑הּ עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֗ר בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ חֶלְמָ֤א וּפִשְׁרֵא֙ אַֽל־יְבַהֲלָ֔ךְ עָנֵ֤ה בֵלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ וְאָמַ֔ר מראי מָרִ֕י חֶלְמָ֥א לשנאיך לְשָֽׂנְאָ֖ךְ וּפִשְׁרֵ֥הּ לעריך לְעָרָֽךְ׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin Dāniyyēʾl dî-šəmēh Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar ʾeštōmam kə-šāʿāh ḥăḏāh wə-raʿyōnōhî yəḇahălunnēh ʿănēh malkāʾ wə-ʾāmar Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar ḥelmāʾ ū-p̄išrēʾ ʾal-yəḇahălāḵ ʿănēh Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar wə-ʾāmar mārî ḥelmāʾ lə-śānʾāḵ ū-p̄išrēh lə-ʿārāḵ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:16 (= English 4:19; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was dismayed for a while, and his thoughts alarmed him. The king said: 'Belteshazzar, let not the dream or the interpretation alarm you.' Belteshazzar answered: 'My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!'** **NARRATIVE SWITCH** to third-person (vv 19-33 cover the period when the king cannot self-narrate due to madness). Daniel's tact: the interpretation is dire, and the wise-courtier convention is to wish the curse on enemies. Qere-ketiv: מראי/מָרִי; לשנאיך/לְשָׂנְאָךְ; לעריך/לְעָרָךְ.

verses.text: אִֽילָנָא֙ דִּ֣י חֲזַ֔יְתָ דִּ֥י רְבָ֖ה וּתְקִ֑ף וְרוּמֵהּ֙ יִמְטֵ֣א לִשְׁמַיָּ֔א וַחֲזוֹתֵ֖הּ לְכָל־אַרְעָֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾîlānāʾ dī ḥăzaytā dī rəḇāh ū-ṯəqip wə-rūmēh yimṭēʾ li-šmayyāʾ wa-ḥăzōṯēh lə-ḵol-ʾarʿāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:17 (= English 4:20; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'The tree you saw, which grew and became strong, so that its top reached to heaven, and it was visible to the end of the whole earth...'** Recapitulation begins.

verses.text: וְעָפְיֵ֤הּ שַׁפִּיר֙ וְאִנְבֵּ֣הּ שַׂגִּ֔יא וּמָז֨וֹן לְכֹ֖לָּא־בֵ֑הּ תְּחֹת֗וֹהִי תְּדוּר֙ חֵיוַ֣ת בָּרָ֔א וּבְעַנְפ֕וֹהִי יִשְׁכְּנָ֖ן צִפֲּרֵ֥י שְׁמַיָּֽא׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿopyēh šappîr wə-ʾinbēh śaggîʾ ū-māzōn lə-ḵōllāʾ-ḇēh təḥōṯōhî təḏūr ḥêwaṯ bārāʾ ū-ḇə-ʿanpōhî yiškənān ṣippărê šəmayyāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:18 (= English 4:21; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'...whose leaves were fair and its fruit abundant, and in which was food for all, under which the beasts of the field dwelt, and in whose branches the birds of the air had their habitation...'**

verses.text: אנתה־ה֣וּא אַנְתְּ־ה֣וּא מַלְכָּ֔א דִּ֥י רְבַ֖ית וּתְקֵ֑פְתְּ וּרְבוּתָ֤ךְ רְבָת֙ וּמְטָ֣ת לִשְׁמַיָּ֔א וְשָׁלְטָנָ֖ךְ לְס֥וֹף אַרְעָֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾant-hūʾ malkāʾ dî rəḇaytā ū-ṯəqēptā ū-rəḇūṯāḵ rəḇāṯ ū-məṭāṯ li-šmayyāʾ wə-šolṭānāḵ lə-sōp̄ ʾarʿāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:19 (= English 4:22; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'It is you, O king, who have grown and become strong; your greatness has grown and reaches to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the earth.'** **THE IDENTIFICATION**: 'you are the tree' — the king IS the cosmic-axis tree. Cf. 2:38 ('you are the head of gold').

verses.text: וְדִ֣י חֲזָ֣ה מַלְכָּ֡א עִ֣יר וְקַדִּ֣ישׁ נָחִ֣ת ׀ מִן־שְׁמַיָּ֡א וְאָמַר֩ גֹּ֨דּוּ אִֽילָנָ֜א וְחַבְּל֗וּהִי בְּרַ֨ם עִקַּ֤ר שָׁרְשׁ֙וֹהִי֙ בְּאַרְעָ֣א שְׁבֻ֔קוּ וּבֶאֱסוּר֙ דִּֽי־פַרְזֶ֣ל וּנְחָ֔שׁ בְּדִתְאָ֖א דִּ֣י בָרָ֑א וּבְטַ֧ל שְׁמַיָּ֣א יִצְטַבַּ֗ע וְעִם־חֵיוַ֤ת בָּרָא֙ חֲלָקֵ֔הּ עַ֛ד דִּֽי־שִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֥וּן עֲלֽוֹהִי׃
verses.translit: wə-ḏî ḥăzāh malkāʾ ʿîr wə-qaddîš nāḥiṯ min-šəmayyāʾ wə-ʾāmar gōddū ʾîlānāʾ wə-ḥabbəlūhî bəram ʿiqqar šoršōhî bə-ʾarʿāʾ šəḇuqū ū-ḇe-ʾĕsūr dî-p̄arzel ū-nəḥāš bə-ḏiṯʾāʾ dī ḇārāʾ ū-ḇə-ṭal šəmayyāʾ yiṣṭabbaʿ wə-ʿim-ḥêwaṯ bārāʾ ḥălāqēh ʿaḏ dî-šiḇʿāh ʿiddānîn yaḥləp̄ūn ʿălōhî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:20 (= English 4:23; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'And as the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying: Cut down the tree and destroy it; but leave the stump of its roots in the earth, bound with a band of iron and bronze, in the tender grass of the field; let him be wet with the dew of heaven; and let his lot be with the beasts of the field till seven times pass over him.'**

verses.text: דְּנָ֥ה פִשְׁרָ֖א מַלְכָּ֑א וּגְזֵרַ֤ת עליא עִלָּאָה֙ הִ֔יא דִּ֥י מְטָ֖ת עַל־מראי מָרִ֥י מַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: dənāh pišrāʾ malkāʾ ū-ḡzēraṯ ʿillāʾāh hîʾ dî məṭāṯ ʿal-mārî malkāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:21 (= English 4:24; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'This is the interpretation, O king: it is a decree of the Most High, which has come upon my lord the king.'** Qere-ketiv: עליא/עִלָּאָה; מראי/מָרִי.

verses.text: וְלָ֣ךְ טָֽרְדִ֣ין מִן־אֲנָשָׁ֡א וְעִם־חֵיוַ֣ת בָּרָא֩ לֶהֱוֵ֨ה מְדֹרָ֜ךְ וְעִשְׂבָּ֥א כְתוֹרִ֣ין ׀ לָ֣ךְ יְטַֽעֲמ֗וּן וּמִטַּ֤ל שְׁמַיָּא֙ לָ֣ךְ מְצַבְּעִ֔ין וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֣וּן עֲלָ֑ךְ עַ֣ד דִּֽי־תִנְדַּ֗ע דִּֽי־שַׁלִּ֤יט עליא עִלָּאָה֙ בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֔א וּלְמַן־דִּ֥י יִצְבֵּ֖א יִתְּנִנַּֽהּ׃
verses.translit: wə-lāḵ ṭārəḏîn min-ʾănāšāʾ wə-ʿim-ḥêwaṯ bārāʾ lehĕwēh mə-ḏōrāḵ wə-ʿiśbāʾ ḵə-ṯōrîn lāḵ yəṭaʿămūn ū-miṭṭal šəmayyāʾ lāḵ məṣabbəʿîn wə-šiḇʿāh ʿiddānîn yaḥləp̄ūn ʿălāḵ ʿaḏ dî-ṯindaʿ dî-šallîṭ ʿillāʾāh bə-malḵūṯ ʾănāšāʾ ū-lə-man-dî yiṣbēʾ yittəninnah
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:22 (= English 4:25; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'You shall be driven from among men, and your dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field; you shall be made to eat grass like an ox, and you shall be wet with the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass over you, till you know that the Most High rules the kingdom of men and gives it to whom he will.'** **THE PURPOSE-CLAUSE**: the madness is purgative-pedagogical — to teach the king the doctrine of divine sovereignty. Repeats v 17 refrain. Qere-ketiv: עליא/עִלָּאָה.

verses.text: וְדִ֣י אֲמַ֗רוּ לְמִשְׁבַּ֛ק עִקַּ֥ר שָׁרְשׁ֖וֹהִי דִּ֣י אִֽילָנָ֑א מַלְכוּתָ֤ךְ לָךְ֙ קַיָּמָ֔ה מִן־דִּ֣י תִנְדַּ֔ע דִּ֥י שַׁלִּטִ֖ן שְׁמַיָּֽא׃
verses.translit: wə-ḏî ʾămarū lə-mišbaq ʿiqqar šoršōhî dî ʾîlānāʾ malḵūṯāḵ lāḵ qayyāmāh min-dî ṯindaʿ dī šalliṭin šəmayyāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:23 (= English 4:26; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'And as it was commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree, your kingdom shall be sure for you from the time that you know that Heaven rules.'** **CROSS-CORPUS — TERMINOLOGY**: שַׁלִּטִן שְׁמַיָּא (šalliṭin šəmayyāʾ 'Heaven rules') — the use of 'Heaven' as a circumlocution for God anticipates the rabbinic מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם / NT βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν 'kingdom of heaven' (Matthew's distinctive phrase). 1 Macc 3:18-19, 4:10 also uses 'Heaven' as divine circumlocution.

verses.text: לָהֵ֣ן מַלְכָּ֗א מִלְכִּי֙ יִשְׁפַּ֣ר עליך עֲלָ֔ךְ וחטיך וַחֲטָאָךְ֙ בְּצִדְקָ֣ה פְרֻ֔ק וַעֲוָיָתָ֖ךְ בְּמִחַ֣ן עֲנָ֑יִן הֵ֛ן תֶּהֱוֵ֥ה אַרְכָ֖ה לִשְׁלֵוְתָֽךְ׃
verses.translit: lāhēn malkāʾ milkî yišpar ʿălāḵ wa-ḥăṭāʾāḵ bə-ṣiḏqāh pəruq wa-ʿăwāyāṯāḵ bə-miḥan ʿănāyin hēn tehĕwēh ʾarḵāh li-šəlēwṯāḵ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:24 (= English 4:27; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you: break off your sins by practicing righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed, that there may perhaps be a lengthening of your tranquility.'** **THE ALMSGIVING-VERSE**: critical for late Second-Temple ethics. The Aramaic צִדְקָה (ṣiḏqāh) here clearly means 'almsgiving' (the post-biblical Aramaic/Hebrew sense — צְדָקָה ṣəḏāqāh = 'charity'). **CROSS-CORPUS**: Tob 4:7-11, 12:8-9 develops alms-as-atonement directly from Dan 4:27. The OG-Greek translates ἐλεημοσύναις 'in almsgivings' — this is the EARLIEST attestation of the alms-as-atonement doctrine that Matthew (Matt 6:1-4) and the entire later Jewish-Christian tradition inherits. The Vulgate's rendering of צִדְקָה as *eleemosynis* is foundational for Catholic almsgiving-doctrine and the Reformation controversy over Tob/Dan-derived works-righteousness. Qere-ketiv: עליך/עֲלָךְ; וחטיך/וַחֲטָאָךְ.

verses.text: כֹּ֖לָּא מְּטָ֑א עַל־נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: kōllāʾ mməṭāʾ ʿal-Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:25 (= English 4:28; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **All this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.** Brief summary heading.

verses.text: לִקְצָ֥ת יַרְחִ֖ין תְּרֵֽי־עֲשַׂ֑ר עַל־הֵיכַ֧ל מַלְכוּתָ֛א דִּ֥י בָבֶ֖ל מְהַלֵּ֥ךְ הֲוָֽה׃
verses.translit: li-qṣāṯ yarḥîn təre-ʿăśar ʿal-hêḵal malḵūṯāʾ dī Bāḇel məhallēḵ hăwāh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:26 (= English 4:29; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **At the end of twelve months he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon.** Twelve-month grace-period between dream and fulfillment. The roof-of-palace setting echoes 2 Sam 11:2 (David on the roof) — the king-on-roof-surveys-domain trope.

verses.text: עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֔ר הֲלָ֥א דָא־הִ֖יא בָּבֶ֣ל רַבְּתָ֑א דִּֽי־אֲנָ֤ה בֱנַיְתַהּ֙ לְבֵ֣ית מַלְכ֔וּ בִּתְקַ֥ף חִסְנִ֖י וְלִיקָ֥ר הַדְרִֽי׃
verses.translit: ʿănēh malkāʾ wə-ʾāmar hălāʾ ḏāʾ-hîʾ Bāḇel rabbəṯāʾ dî-ʾănāh ḇĕnaytah lə-ḇêṯ malḵū bi-ṯqap̄ ḥisnî wə-lî-qār haḏrî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:27 (= English 4:30; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **The king said: 'Is not this great Babylon, which I have built by my mighty power as a royal residence and for the glory of my majesty?'** **THE HUBRIS-DECLARATION**: the trigger for the curse. Historically, Nebuchadnezzar II did undertake massive building-works in Babylon (Ishtar Gate, Etemenanki ziggurat, Hanging Gardens, processional way), all attested in cuneiform inscriptions. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Isa 14 (Day Star/king-of-Babylon hubris-fall); cf. Rev 18 ('Babylon the great') — direct verbal echo. The Greek of Rev 18:10 quotes precisely 'Babylon the great' (Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη) — the Aramaic בָּבֶל רַבְּתָא (Bāḇel rabbəṯāʾ) feeds directly into Revelation's Roman-Babylon.

verses.text: ע֗וֹד מִלְּתָא֙ בְּפֻ֣ם מַלְכָּ֔א קָ֖ל מִן־שְׁמַיָּ֣א נְפַ֑ל לָ֤ךְ אָֽמְרִין֙ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֔א מַלְכוּתָ֖ה עֲדָ֥ת מִנָּֽךְ׃
verses.translit: ʿōḏ milləṯāʾ bə-p̄um malkāʾ qāl min-šəmayyāʾ nəp̄al lāḵ ʾāmərîn Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ malḵūṯāh ʿăḏāṯ minnāḵ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:28 (= English 4:31; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **While the words were still in the king's mouth, a voice fell from heaven: 'O King Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: The kingdom has departed from you.'** **THE BAT-QOL** (heavenly voice) motif: pre-rabbinic instance. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Mark 1:11 / Matt 3:17 / Luke 3:22 (the bat-qol at Jesus' baptism); cf. Acts 9:4 (the Damascus-road voice).

verses.text: וּמִן־אֲנָשָׁא֩ לָ֨ךְ טָֽרְדִ֜ין וְֽעִם־חֵיוַ֧ת בָּרָ֣א מְדֹרָ֗ךְ עִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ לָ֣ךְ יְטַֽעֲמ֔וּן וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֣וּן עליך עֲלָ֑ךְ עַ֣ד דִּֽי־תִנְדַּ֗ע דִּֽי־שַׁלִּ֤יט עליא עִלָּאָה֙ בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֔א וּלְמַן־דִּ֥י יִצְבֵּ֖א יִתְּנִנַּֽהּ׃
verses.translit: ū-min-ʾănāšāʾ lāḵ ṭārəḏîn wə-ʿim-ḥêwaṯ bārāʾ mə-ḏōrāḵ ʿiśbāʾ ḵə-ṯōrîn lāḵ yəṭaʿămūn wə-šiḇʿāh ʿiddānîn yaḥləp̄ūn ʿălāḵ ʿaḏ dî-ṯindaʿ dî-šallîṭ ʿillāʾāh bə-malḵūṯ ʾănāšāʾ ū-lə-man-dî yiṣbēʾ yittəninnah
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:29 (= English 4:32; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'And you shall be driven from among men, and your dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field; you shall be made to eat grass like an ox; and seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules the kingdom of men and gives it to whom he will.'** Qere-ketiv (twice): עליך/עֲלָךְ; עליא/עִלָּאָה.

verses.text: בַּהּ־שַׁעֲתָ֗א מִלְּתָא֮ סָ֣פַת עַל־נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר֒ וּמִן־אֲנָשָׁ֣א טְרִ֔יד וְעִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ יֵאכֻ֔ל וּמִטַּ֥ל שְׁמַיָּ֖א גִּשְׁמֵ֣הּ יִצְטַבַּ֑ע עַ֣ד דִּ֥י שַׂעְרֵ֛הּ כְּנִשְׁרִ֥ין רְבָ֖ה וְטִפְר֥וֹהִי כְצִפְּרִֽין׃
verses.translit: bah-šaʿăṯāʾ millə-ṯāʾ sāp̄aṯ ʿal-Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar ū-min-ʾănāšāʾ ṭərîḏ wə-ʿiśbāʾ ḵə-ṯōrîn yêḵul ū-miṭṭal šəmayyāʾ gišmēh yiṣṭabbaʿ ʿaḏ dī śaʿrēh kə-nišrîn rəḇāh wə-ṭipprōhî ḵə-ṣipprîn
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:30 (= English 4:33; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Immediately the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from among men, and ate grass like an ox, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hair grew as long as eagles' feathers, and his nails were like birds' claws.** **THE BOANTHROPY/LYCANTHROPY-DESCRIPTION**: clinical lycanthropy is a recognized rare psychiatric syndrome. The exact features described — long hair, claw-like nails, eating-grass, outdoor dwelling — match the literary trope of the 'wild man' (cf. Enkidu in Gilgamesh; Nebuchadnezzar here is being reduced toward an Enkidu-state, an inversion of civilization). Historically, Nabonidus (not Nebuchadnezzar) spent 553-543 BCE at Teima — the 4Q242 Prayer of Nabonidus likely preserves the historical core.

verses.text: וְלִקְצָ֣ת יֽוֹמַיָּה֩ אֲנָ֨ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֜ר עַיְנַ֣י ׀ לִשְׁמַיָּ֣א נִטְלֵ֗ת וּמַנְדְּעִי֙ עֲלַ֣י יְת֔וּב ולעליא וּלְעִלָּאָה֙ בָּרְכֵ֔ת וּלְחַ֥י עָלְמָ֖א שַׁבְּחֵ֣ת וְהַדְּרֵ֑ת דִּ֤י שָׁלְטָנֵהּ֙ שָׁלְטָ֣ן עָלַ֔ם וּמַלְכוּתֵ֖הּ עִם־דָּ֥ר וְדָֽר׃
verses.translit: wə-li-qṣāṯ yōmayyāh ʾănāh Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar ʿaynay li-šmayyāʾ niṭlēṯ ū-mandəʿî ʿălay yəṯūḇ ū-lə-ʿillāʾāh bārəḵēṯ ū-lə-ḥay ʿāləmāʾ šabbəḥēṯ wə-haddərēṯ dī šolṭānēh šolṭān ʿālam ū-malḵūṯēh ʿim-dār wə-ḏār
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:31 (= English 4:34; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason returned to me; and I blessed the Most High, and praised and honored him who lives forever; for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation.** **RETURN TO FIRST PERSON**: the narrative resumes Nebuchadnezzar's own voice. **TITLE**: חַי עָלְמָא (ḥay ʿāləmāʾ 'the one who lives forever' / 'the Eternally-Living') — Aramaic equivalent of אֵל חַי / אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 4:9, 10:6, 15:7 (τὸν ζῶντα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων 'the one who lives forever and ever') — direct Aramaic-Daniel inheritance. The everlasting-kingdom refrain repeats. Qere-ketiv: ולעליא/וּלְעִלָּאָה.

verses.text: וְכָל־דָּאֲרֵ֤י אַרְעָא֙ כְּלָ֣ה חֲשִׁיבִ֔ין וּֽכְמִצְבְּיֵ֗הּ עָבֵד֙ בְּחֵ֣יל שְׁמַיָּ֔א ודארי וְדָיְרֵ֖י אַרְעָ֑א וְלָ֤א אִיתַי֙ דִּֽי־יְמַחֵ֣א בִידֵ֔הּ וְיֵ֥אמַר לֵ֖הּ מָ֥ה עֲבַֽדְתְּ׃
verses.translit: wə-ḵol-dāʾărê ʾarʿāʾ kə-lāh ḥăšîḇîn ū-ḵə-miṣbəyēh ʿāḇēḏ bə-ḥêl šəmayyāʾ wə-ḏāyərê ʾarʿāʾ wə-lāʾ ʾîtay dî-yəmaḥēʾ ḇi-yḏēh wə-yêmar lēh māh ʿăḇaḏt
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:32 (= English 4:35; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **All the inhabitants of the earth are accounted as nothing; he does according to his will in the host of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth; and none can stay his hand or say to him: What are you doing?** **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Isa 40:17 ('all the nations are as nothing'); cf. Isa 45:9, Job 9:12 ('who can say to him: What are you doing?') — the doctrine of unimpedable divine sovereignty. Rom 9:20 ('who are you, O man, to answer back to God?') directly inherits the Daniel-Aramaic challenge-question. Qere-ketiv: ודארי/וְדָיְרֵי.

verses.text: בֵּהּ־זִמְנָ֞א מַנְדְּעִ֣י ׀ יְת֣וּב עֲלַ֗י וְלִיקַ֨ר מַלְכוּתִ֤י הַדְרִי֙ וְזִוִ֣י יְת֣וּב עֲלַ֔י וְלִ֕י הַדָּֽבְרַ֥י וְרַבְרְבָנַ֖י יְבַע֑וֹן וְעַל־מַלְכוּתִ֣י הָתְקְנַ֔ת וּרְב֥וּ יַתִּירָ֖ה ה֥וּסְפַת לִֽי׃
verses.translit: bēh-zimnāʾ mandəʿî yəṯūḇ ʿălay wə-lî-qar malḵūṯî haḏrî wə-zîwî yəṯūḇ ʿălay wə-lî haddāḇəray wə-raḇrəḇānay yəḇaʿōn wə-ʿal-malḵūṯî hoṯqənaṯ ū-rəḇū yattîrāh hūspaṯ lî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:33 (= English 4:36; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **At the same time my reason returned to me; and for the glory of my kingdom, my majesty and splendor returned to me; my counselors and my lords sought me, I was established in my kingdom, and surpassing greatness was added to me.** The Joseph-pattern restoration (after testing → exalted state).

verses.text: כְּעַ֞ן אֲנָ֣ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר מְשַׁבַּ֨ח וּמְרוֹמֵ֤ם וּמְהַדַּר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ שְׁמַיָּ֔א דִּ֤י כָל־מַעֲבָד֙וֹהִי קְשֹׁ֔ט וְאֹרְחָתֵ֖הּ דִּ֑ין וְדִי֙ מַהְלְכִ֣ין בְּגֵוָ֔ה יָכִ֖ל לְהַשְׁפָּלָֽה׃
verses.translit: kəʿan ʾănāh Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar məšabbaḥ ū-mərōmēm ū-məhaddar lə-meleḵ šəmayyāʾ dī ḵol-maʿăḇāḏōhî qəšōṭ wə-ʾorḥāṯēh dîn wə-ḏî mahləḵîn bə-ḡēwāh yāḵil lə-hašpālāh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 4:34 (= English 4:37; Aramaic)
verses.witness_tertiary: OG ends the chapter with a substantially different concluding doxology
verses.notes: **Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honor the King of heaven, for all his works are right and his ways are just; and those who walk in pride he is able to abase.** **TITLE**: מֶלֶךְ שְׁמַיָּא (meleḵ šəmayyāʾ 'King of heaven') — appears here uniquely in HB. **CROSS-CORPUS**: foundational for the rabbinic 'King of kings' formula + Matthew's 'kingdom of heaven' terminology. cf. 1 Tim 1:17 ('King of the ages'); cf. Rev 15:3 ('King of the ages/nations'). **CHAPTER-ENDING — THE GENTILE CONVERSION-TESTIMONY**: the Babylonian king publicly testifies to YHWH's sovereignty — the climactic narrative-theological move of the Aramaic chs 2-7 cycle. Historically, no extra-biblical record corroborates Nebuchadnezzar's conversion; this is theological-literary.
